scoring_notes: Missed black widow can delay medical advice for clinically significant Latrodectus envenomation; moderate symptoms can require medication/observation and rare major effects occur.
False alarm mainly causes caution, anxiety, or evaluation; Steatoda bites are not treated as harmless, but public evidence does not support Latrodectus-level morbidity.

Missed malignancy can delay treatment, permit progression, and is time-sensitive; screening and pathology-adjacent evidence are used because no BreaKHis-specific cost matrix exists. Threshold estimator 9 corresponds to an exact 10% action threshold.
False malignant support can cause anxiety and additional workup, but in the intended decision-support setting it should trigger review rather than autonomous cancer treatment.
